Smokey then revealed that his wife called him crying about Michael dying, which you can hear more about above.

The incident caused serious burns and required a long recovery. Despite the trauma, Michael Jackson made a powerful decision afterward—he donated the full $1.5 million settlement from Pepsi to help establish the Michael Jackson Burn Center. What began as a tragic accident ultimately became a source of hope and treatment for burn victims around the world.

The Day Michael Jackson Caught Fire – The Shocking Truth Behind the 1984 Pepsi Commercial Incident

On January 27, 1984, Michael Jackson, the King of Pop, suffered a tragic and life-altering accident that would haunt him for the rest of his life. During the filming of a Pepsi commercial at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles, a pyrotechnics mishap caused his hair to catch fire. The accident occurred on the sixth take when sparks from a fireworks display ignited Michael's scalp as he descended a staircase on stage.

What began as a high-profile brand collaboration turned into a horrifying emergency. Michael suffered second- and third-degree burns to his scalp and face, leaving him in excruciating pain. He continued performing for several seconds, unaware that his head was engulfed in flames, until crew members rushed to extinguish the fire.

This traumatic event had long-term consequences. Many believe the pain and subsequent medical treatments—including powerful painkillers—contributed to Jackson’s later struggles with dependency and health issues. Though he recovered physically and even continued performing, the emotional and psychological scars remained.

This short unpacks one of the most disturbing and lesser-known moments in pop culture history—a reminder that even icons carry unseen pain.

On January 27, 1984, Michael Jackson, the King of Pop, suffered a tragic and life-altering accident that would haunt him for the rest of his life. During the filming of a Pepsi commercial at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles, a pyrotechnics mishap caused his hair to catch fire. The accident occurred on the sixth take when sparks from a fireworks display ignited Michael's scalp as he descended a staircase on stage.

What began as a high-profile brand collaboration turned into a horrifying emergency. Michael suffered second- and third-degree burns to his scalp and face, leaving him in excruciating pain. He continued performing for several seconds, unaware that his head was engulfed in flames, until crew members rushed to extinguish the fire.

This traumatic event had long-term consequences. Many believe the pain and subsequent medical treatments—including powerful painkillers—contributed to Jackson’s later struggles with dependency and health issues. Though he recovered physically and even continued performing, the emotional and psychological scars remained.

This short unpacks one of the most disturbing and lesser-known moments in pop culture history—a reminder that even icons carry unseen pain.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson PEPSI Commercial Accident - ALL ANGLES Synced to Original Audio!
snippet.description:
#video #music #michaeljackson  A horrific incident, undoubtedly adversely affecting the trajectory of MJ's life, and arguably catalyzing his ultimate tragic downfall.

Split screen.

No copyright infringement intended.

Copied from the Michael Jackson Wiki:

On January 27, 1984, Michael Jackson was filming a Pepsi commercial at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles alongside his brothers from The Jacksons. The commercial was produced as part of a multi-million dollar endorsement deal with PepsiCo, which sought to capitalize on Jackson’s immense popularity at the time. The filming took place before a live audience, creating the atmosphere of a concert performance. 

Background & Incident:
During the sixth take of the shoot, a pyrotechnic malfunction occurred as Jackson descended a staircase while performing. The premature explosion of fireworks ignited his heavily gelled hair, resulting in second-degree burns to his scalp. As the flames spread, Jackson continued to perform for a few seconds before realizing something was wrong. Crew members and handlers immediately rushed to extinguish the flames and assist him.

Following the accident, Jackson received medical treatment for his injuries. The burns led to significant scarring, and he later underwent several medical procedures, including treatments to conceal the damage. Shortly after the incident, he also underwent his third rhinoplasty.

The commercial, overseen by Phil Dusenberry (a creative executive at the BBDO advertising agency) and Alan Pottasch (Pepsi's Worldwide Creative Director), was eventually completed and aired, despite the accident.

Reaction

Katherine Jackson’s Reaction:
Jackson’s mother, Katherine Jackson, was deeply upset upon learning about the accident. She was particularly angered by the lack of safety precautions that led to her son’s injury and strongly considered taking legal action against Pepsi. Michael himself also expressed frustration and reportedly threatened to sue the company. As a mother, Katherine was not only concerned about Michael’s physical well-being but also about the emotional toll the incident might take on him.

Legal Settlement & Philanthropic Impact:
Rather than pursuing legal action, Jackson and Pepsi reached a settlement out of court. PepsiCo agreed to pay Jackson $1.5 million (equivalent to $4.4 million in 2023). In a generous act of philanthropy, Jackson donated the entire settlement to the Brotman Medical Center in Culver City, California, which later established the Michael Jackson Burn Center in his honor.

Despite the accident, Jackson maintained a working relationship with Pepsi. In the late 1980s, he signed a second endorsement deal worth $10 million (approximately $26.8 million in 2023). This new agreement covered promotional campaigns across 20 countries and helped finance his Bad album and Bad World Tour (1987-88). Though Jackson had endorsement deals with other companies, including LA Gear, Suzuki, and Sony, none were as impactful or lucrative as his partnership with Pepsi.

Aftermath:
In the years following the accident Jackson’s hairstylist, Carol LaMere, played a significant role in helping him manage the damage caused by the burns. 

She later recounted her experience working with Jackson:
”I was recommended to him by a mutual friend. I was driven to his home and he came into the car and introduced himself. He showed me where he had been burned. It really was not bad at the beginning. It was like two eggs in size and was towards the back. However, he still had a huge head of hair surrounding it. However, he was self-conscious, which was common for those in his line of work."

Contrary to popular belief, LaMere clarified that Jackson rarely wore wigs:
”Despite what many people might think, I very rarely, if ever, resorted to wigs for him. I remember many commenting on him wearing a wig for Remember the Time. It wasn’t. All it was was a hairpiece with a few extensions. When he was touring it was easier, especially for his Dangerous and History tours. He grew his actual hair very long and we were able to comb that back into a bun or ponytail to cover it. The only time he wore a hair piece was for Black or White because he preferred his hair down for that song.”

However, Jackson’s hair loss worsened over time due to multiple unsuccessful surgical procedures intended to repair the damage. These operations only further depleted his natural hair, leading him to explore other cosmetic solutions.

”It did become a little harder to manage before I left because he had several surgeries to try and fix it. Several doctors made him promises that it could be done but all it did was rob him of more of his natural hair. I heard stories from those working with him before his passing that he tattooed his head to cover up his receding hairline. That actually upset me. I’ve had other clients do that but all that does is kill the hair follicles even further, which broke my heart because he did have hair.”
